derived_insights: Allowing min_replicas=0 frequently causes brief under-provisioning during sudden bursts; set region-specific minimums for high-traffic routes.
Short cooldowns (<=30s) reduce peak latency faster but induce oscillation for noisy workloads; 45-90s is a safer middle ground for most models.
Higher scale_up_qps thresholds reduce cost but increase tail latency during peaks — critical customer routes should use lower thresholds and slightly higher mins.
Burst pools (separate max pool) are effective for predictable daily spikes but require explicit cost accounting — recommend tagging burst routes and limiting frequency.
Quantized small-batch workloads are sensitive to undersized mins; batching improves utilization but min>=2 reduces queueing significantly.
summary_recommendation: Region-by-region defaults: us-west1 (min=1 for most, min=2 for heavy models), us-east4 (min=2 for critical routes), eu-west1 (min=2 for quantized models), ap-southeast1 (min=1 but increase cooldown to 60s). Standardize cooldown to 45s for general-purpose profiles; lower to 30s for highly predictable traffic. Use burst pools for scheduled spikes only; tag routes for cost tracking.
